title: Gatsby Begins: Nick Arrives and Points East
adaptation_scope: Opening narration through Nick’s move to West Egg, early summer settling-in, and spatial orientation culminating in the reveal of Gatsby’s mansion.

style_bible.visual_period: Midwest retrospective (post-1922) contrasted with Spring–Summer 1922 Long Island; brief 1910s Yale/Great War flashes.
style_bible.line_and_color: Clean, expressive line; period-accurate detail. TF1 cooler/sepia undertones; TF2–TF4 warmer greens and golds with crisp coastal blues.
style_bible.lighting: TF1: desk lamplight and window glow; TF2–TF4: bright spring/summer daylight; TF4 mansion views at late afternoon/dusk for contrast.
style_bible.lettering: Narration in understated serif caption boxes; dialogue minimal in clean mixed-case; SFX sparing and quiet. Color cue captions: cooler tint for TF1.
recurring_motifs: Nick’s hand and notebook under lamplight
Fast-growing spring leaves and moving air
Nick pointing or framing vistas with his arm

characters.name: Nick Carraway
characters.visual_anchor: Neat, modest Midwesterner; clean part; thoughtful eyes; often holding a notebook or looking outward.
characters.costume: Simple suits, shirt-sleeves at desk; 1922 casual jacket and tie outdoors.
characters.expression_range: Reserved, observant; faint smiles; introspective distance; occasional wryness.
characters.continuity_note: Dual presence: TF1 as retrospective writer at desk in cooler palette; TF2–TF4 as active observer in warmer tones.

characters.name: Nick’s Father
characters.visual_anchor: Soft-edged memory figure; older gentleman with calm gaze.
characters.continuity_note: Appears only as a ghosted memory in TF1; never fully solid or over-defined.

characters.name: Coworker
characters.visual_anchor: Cheerful, well-meaning office man, shirtsleeves, tie loosened.
characters.continuity_note: Brief presence: pitches house-share, then exits to Washington; no dialogue text.

characters.name: Finnish Woman (Housekeeper)
characters.visual_anchor: Middle-aged, practical, hair in bun, focused on stove.
characters.continuity_note: Shown minimally to texture Nick’s domestic setup.

characters.name: Anonymous Neighbor (Directions)
characters.visual_anchor: Harmless newcomer, slightly lost, hat in hand by the roadside.
characters.continuity_note: One line only: asks the way to West Egg village.

characters.name: Jay Gatsby (implied)
characters.visual_anchor: Never directly seen; presence felt via colossal mansion and lawns.
characters.continuity_note: Maintain mystery—no direct depiction of Gatsby himself in this sequence.

pages.page_summary: Nick’s reflective frame launches; his habit of reserving judgment and its limit; a first, distant nod toward Gatsby.

panels.character_action: At a desk in later years, Nick opens his notebook and recalls his father’s words.
panels.beat: Nick writes and recalls his father’s advice.
panels.image_prompt: Interior night, Midwestern study with warm lamplight. Nick, late-twenties/early-thirties, leans over an open notebook, pen poised. Over-the-shoulder angle with his hand and the blank page in foreground. A soft, translucent memory image of an older gentleman (his father) behind him. No readable text anywhere; no captions or lettering; quiet, reflective mood.
panels.caption: My father taught me not to judge people too quickly.
panels.continuity_notes: TF1 palette: cooler/sepia undertone; lamplight glow; father only as ghosted memory.
panels.lettering_notes: Top left caption; avoid Nick's face.
panels.adaptation_note: B1 covers source units 1–3; unit 3 implied in Nick’s expression.

panels.character_action: Younger Nick sits listening as a roommate leans in with a midnight confession.
panels.beat: Nick’s habit of reserving judgment draws confidences.
panels.image_prompt: Dormitory or boarding room at night; younger Nick half-lit on bunk, an eager roommate leaning in to confide. Coffee cup, rumpled blanket. No readable text, no captions in art.
panels.caption: That habit made other men trust me with their secrets.
panels.continuity_notes: Still TF1 narration over past vignette; keep montage feel.
panels.lettering_notes: Top left caption; avoid both faces.
panels.adaptation_note: B2 uses unit 4; units 5–6 implied visually later; keep text minimal.

panels.character_action: On a night train, Nick feigns sleep to avoid another confider.
panels.beat: Trait-in-action, with wary tolerance.
panels.image_prompt: Night train club car; Nick reclines with eyes shut as a stranger hovers uncertainly, about to speak. Passing lights streak the windows. No readable text, no labels, no captions in art.
panels.caption: I did not always want those secrets, but I still tried to reserve judgment.
panels.continuity_notes: Thin horizontal montage vibe; TF1 captions continue.
panels.lettering_notes: Top left caption; use the window space.
panels.adaptation_note: B2 covers units 7–8 text; units 5–6 (confidences) shown silently.

panels.character_action: Back in the Midwest after the East, Nick turns down a lively invitation and closes his door.
panels.beat: Nick’s limit to tolerance after returning from the East.
panels.image_prompt: Interior hallway with warm party light and silhouettes spilling from a distant room; Nick’s hand turns his doorknob to shut out the noise. Cooler, tidier room beyond. No readable text.
panels.caption: After I came back from the East, I wanted the world to stand at moral attention.
panels.continuity_notes: Shift to cooler palette within TF1 to cue austerity.
panels.lettering_notes: Top right caption; keep off the hand and party figures.
panels.adaptation_note: B3 folds unit 10 into 9 via this single line.

panels.character_action: Nick pauses at a window, gazing toward distant water; a lone figure stands far off on a dock.
panels.beat: Gatsby as exception begins to take shape.
panels.image_prompt: Interior window view to a shoreline at dusk; Nick’s reflection faint in the glass; across the water a tiny solitary figure on a dock suggests distance and mystery. No readable text.
panels.caption: Only Gatsby escaped my disgust.
panels.continuity_notes: Keep the distant figure generic; do not reveal Gatsby.
panels.lettering_notes: Top right caption; keep off Nick's reflected face.
panels.adaptation_note: B4 begins with unit 12 hook to set exception.

pages.page_summary: Gatsby’s ‘gift for hope’ and foreshadowed ruin; Nick’s Midwestern pedigree and decisive move East in spring ’22.

panels.character_action: Still at the window, Nick considers Gatsby’s allure.
panels.beat: Gatsby’s ‘something gorgeous’ and romantic readiness.
panels.image_prompt: Nick’s face reflected over dark glass; subtle shimmer of water beyond; a hint of starry sky. No readable text.
panels.caption: I saw in Gatsby an extraordinary gift for hope.
panels.continuity_notes: Maintain TF1 tone; keep imagery abstract.
panels.lettering_notes: Low right caption; use the water and avoid Nick's face.

panels.character_action: Nick turns from the window, weighed by memory.
panels.beat: Foreshadowing: Gatsby ‘all right’; the foul dust.
panels.image_prompt: Interior shadow as Nick steps away from the window; lamplight behind him; outside remains indistinct. No readable text.
panels.caption: I thought Gatsby was all right; the corruption around his dream was not.
panels.continuity_notes: End TF1 arc; prepare transition to backstory (TF2).
panels.lettering_notes: Top right caption; avoid Nick's body.

panels.character_action: Nick handles a family portrait and suitcase in a Midwestern parlor.
panels.beat: Prominent Middle Western roots.
panels.image_prompt: Sepia-toned Midwestern sitting room; framed family portrait on wall; Nick lifts a suitcase from beside a sturdy chair. No readable text.
panels.caption: I came from a well-to-do Midwestern family.
panels.continuity_notes: TF2 begins; cooler/sepia tone signals past.
panels.lettering_notes: Low left caption; use the chair area and avoid the portrait and Nick.

panels.character_action: Nick passes a Yale cap on a hook; a flash of trench memory overlays his profile.
panels.beat: Yale ’15 and the Great War; postwar restlessness.
panels.image_prompt: Hallway hook with a Yale cap; faint overlay of a war trench flare behind Nick’s thoughtful profile. No readable text, no insignia detail beyond generic cap.
panels.caption: I went to Yale, served in the war, and came home restless.
panels.continuity_notes: Still TF2; keep trench cue brief, non-graphic.
panels.lettering_notes: Top left caption; use the empty hook area.
panels.adaptation_note: B5 implies units 17–18 without new text.

panels.character_action: On a station platform, Nick takes a ticket from his father and boards an eastbound train.
panels.beat: Decision to learn bonds; financed; arrival timing.
panels.image_prompt: Early spring light at a train platform; handshake between Nick and his father as Nick turns toward the train steps. No readable text on tickets, signs, or cars.
panels.caption: My father financed my move East to learn bonds in spring 1922.
panels.continuity_notes: Transition from sepia to warmer tones as the train departs.
panels.lettering_notes: Top left caption; use the sky and avoid the handshake.
panels.adaptation_note: B5 lands units 19–20 with the time-stamp line.

pages.page_summary: Nick’s West Egg lodging setup: the foiled house-share, threadbare domesticity, and a small roadside encounter that flips his mood.

panels.character_action: At the bond office, Nick listens as a coworker enthusiastically pitches sharing a commuting house.
panels.beat: The appealing plan.
panels.image_prompt: 1922 office floor: desks, ticker tape machine, men in shirtsleeves; coworker gesturing toward a newspaper rental listing (unreadable). Nick considers. No readable text.
panels.caption: A man at the office and I planned to share a house near the city.
panels.continuity_notes: TF3 present-day warmth begins.
panels.lettering_notes: Top left caption; keep above faces.
panels.adaptation_note: B6 sets unit 21 visually per guidance.

panels.character_action: Nick stands at a weather-beaten bungalow as the coworker waves goodbye from a departing car.
panels.beat: Left solo in the $80 bungalow.
panels.image_prompt: Shabby coastal bungalow with peeling paint; a coworker waves from a car pulling away; Nick with suitcase on the small porch. No readable numbers, signs, or labels.
panels.caption: I went out alone when my coworker was sent to Washington.
panels.continuity_notes: Introduce Nick’s bungalow per continuity; near-water feel.
panels.lettering_notes: Top right caption; use the sky and roof area.
panels.adaptation_note: B6 completes unit 22 consequence without added text.

panels.character_action: Nick parks his old Dodge; inside, a Finnish woman fusses at an electric stove as a small dog darts out.
panels.beat: Threadbare domestic texture.
panels.image_prompt: Drive up to the bungalow: weathered car (old Dodge) settling at the curb; inside through open door, a Finnish housekeeper busy at a small electric stove; a little dog streaks past Nick’s legs toward the yard. No readable text.
panels.caption: I kept an old Dodge, a housekeeper, and briefly a dog.
panels.continuity_notes: Keep house modest; emphasize routine and thrift.
panels.lettering_notes: Top left caption; use the tree and car area.

panels.character_action: On a leafy roadside, a lost newcomer hails Nick.
panels.beat: Directions request establishes human contact.
panels.image_prompt: Country road lined with fresh spring leaves; Nick pauses mid-walk as a polite, slightly helpless man gestures, hat in hand. No readable signage or text.
panels.caption: A newer arrival stopped me on the road and asked the way to West Egg village.
panels.continuity_notes: Bright, buoyant morning light to cue summer mood.
panels.lettering_notes: Low left caption; keep off both faces.
panels.adaptation_note: B8 covers units 24–25 with the one allowed line.

panels.character_action: Nick points the way down the road and steps off, lighter.
panels.beat: Shift from isolation to belonging begins.
panels.image_prompt: Nick’s outstretched arm indicates a turn amid sunlit trees; motion in leaves suggests fast growth. No readable text.
panels.caption: I told him, and I felt lonely no longer.
panels.continuity_notes: Start of captioned inner turn; carry momentum into next page.
panels.lettering_notes: Top left caption; use leaves and road space.

pages.page_summary: Belonging crystallizes; Nick’s self-improvement kick with ‘new money’ books and his credo; he begins to orient the Eggs from the shore.

panels.character_action: Walking on, Nick smiles to himself, stride easy under bursting leaves.
panels.beat: Self-mock-heroic flourish of belonging.
panels.image_prompt: Side view of Nick striding along the country lane; sun flares through fast-growing leaves; distant rooftops hint at neighborhood. No readable text.
panels.caption: I felt like a guide, a pathfinder, an original settler.
panels.continuity_notes: Sustain bright early-summer palette.
panels.lettering_notes: Top center caption; use sky and leaves.

panels.character_action: Nick pockets his hands and looks around, at ease among houses and hedges.
panels.beat: Freedom of the neighborhood; summer’s restart.
panels.image_prompt: Neighborhood edge: hedges, porches, a glimpse of the Sound beyond. Nick relaxed, taking it in. No readable text.
panels.caption: With summer beginning, I felt the neighborhood open to me.
panels.continuity_notes: Tie motion of leaves to the summer line subtly.
panels.lettering_notes: Top left caption; use the sky and water.

panels.character_action: Nick sets gleaming red-and-gold banking books onto a shelf.
panels.beat: Finance books like ‘new money.’
panels.image_prompt: Close-up of red-and-gold book spines catching warm light as Nick’s fingers slide a volume into place. No readable titles or text.
panels.caption: I bought books on banking and credit for my new work.
panels.continuity_notes: Warm interior links TF3 present to TF1 study feel.
panels.lettering_notes: Top left caption; use book spines, no faces present.

panels.character_action: At his small desk, Nick pins an old Yale clipping near the shelf and looks satisfied.
panels.beat: Literary past and credo of the ‘well-rounded man.’
panels.image_prompt: Bungalow interior: small desk, shelf with the red-and-gold books, a thumbtacked newspaper clipping (no legible text). No readable text anywhere.
panels.caption: I wanted to become well-rounded again.
panels.continuity_notes: Keep props modest; avoid readable print.
panels.lettering_notes: Top right caption; keep off Nick's head and body.

panels.character_action: Nick walks out to the shoreline, raising an arm to frame the two headlands across the bay.
panels.beat: Begin orienting the Eggs from Nick’s POV.
panels.image_prompt: Long Island Sound shore; Nick in foreground gesturing across water to two curving peninsulas with distinct vibes. No maps, no labels, no text.
panels.caption: From the shore, I saw the two Eggs across the bay.
panels.continuity_notes: Keep geography grounded in Nick’s line of sight.
panels.lettering_notes: Top left caption; use sky and water.
panels.adaptation_note: B10 introduces units 34–35 visually and 37 textually, with 36 implied.

pages.page_summary: Nick completes the orientation: West vs East Egg, his squeezed cottage, and the colossal neighbor revealed as Gatsby’s mansion.

panels.character_action: Nick points to the nearer shore on his side, then across to the other.
panels.beat: Nick places himself in West Egg, the less fashionable.
panels.image_prompt: Shoreline perspective from Nick’s stance: modest houses and new-money bravado on one side, more austere elegance across the water. No readable text.
panels.caption: I lived in West Egg, the less fashionable side.
panels.continuity_notes: Architecture and lawn vibes carry the contrast; no map devices.
panels.lettering_notes: Top left caption; use sky.

panels.character_action: From his front step, Nick glances left and right at the looming neighboring estates; the water glints ahead.
panels.beat: Nick’s cottage squeezed between palaces near the tip.
panels.image_prompt: Tiny weather-beaten cottage foreground; sprawling lawns and large houses flanking left and right; a strip of the Sound sparkles fifty yards ahead. No readable text.
panels.caption: My little house was squeezed between two enormous rented estates.
panels.continuity_notes: Emphasize scale contrast and proximity to water.
panels.lettering_notes: Top left caption; use sky and lawn edge.

panels.character_action: Through a hedge gap, Nick studies the colossal Norman pastiche next door.
panels.beat: The grand neighbor appears.
panels.image_prompt: Vast estate with a newly built Norman ‘Hôtel de Ville’ imitation: towered facade, vast lawns, marble pool glimpsed. Raw ivy just starting along stone. No readable text.
panels.caption: I saw a huge new house made to look like old Normandy.
panels.continuity_notes: Keep mansion spanking new; Gatsby unseen.
panels.lettering_notes: Top left caption; use sky and roofline.

panels.character_action: Nick leans to take in the tower’s raw ivy and the marble pool beyond.
panels.beat: Ownership named—without knowing the man.
panels.image_prompt: Detail of the mansions’s tower profile with a thin beard of raw ivy; bright marble pool beyond manicured lawn. No readable text.
panels.caption: I knew only that it was Gatsby's mansion.
panels.continuity_notes: Preserve mystery: no figure on grounds.
panels.lettering_notes: Top left caption; use mansion wall and water.

panels.character_action: From his porch rail, Nick takes in the Sound and a slice of the neighbor’s immaculate lawn.
panels.beat: Nick’s small eyesore with million-dollar views.
panels.image_prompt: Nick leaning on the tiny cottage porch rail; horizon of the Sound; the neighboring manicured green intrudes into the frame. Golden-hour light. No readable text.
panels.caption: My house was ugly, but it gave me water views and millionaire neighbors for eighty dollars a month.
panels.continuity_notes: End with warm, ironic note; set stage for social world to come.
panels.lettering_notes: Top left caption; keep above Nick's shoulders.
panels.adaptation_note: B13 covers unit 43 exactly; closes orientation.

open_questions: Degree of TF1 vs TF2–TF4 color separation: how cool should TF1 captions appear to the reader without distracting?
Panel 23–24: If space tightens later, should the mansion’s wide and tower-detail compress into a single panel with an inset without losing clarity?
B2 confidences: Are two montage panels sufficient to sell Nick’s listener role, or do we need a third thin inset later for rhythm?
B9 credo: Keep both ‘well-rounded man’ and ‘single window’ in one panel or split if readability demands?
Shoreline orientation (B10): Is the architectural vibe contrast strong enough without any labels, or should Nick’s pointing gesture be exaggerated slightly for clarity?

rules: Every panel has exactly one first-person Nick narration caption.
Captions follow abridged book order panel by panel.
No speech balloons unless a later stage can confidently anchor the speaker to a visible person.
Use simple language and avoid covering faces or major bodies.
